population.span: In this double-blind, randomized trial, we assigned patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric chronic kidney disease to receive canagliflozin, an oral SGLT2 inhibitor, at a dose of 100 mg daily or placebo.

endpoint.span: The primary outcome was a composite of end-stage kidney disease (dialysis, transplantation, or a sustained estimated GFR of <15 ml per minute per 1.73 m2), a doubling of the serum creatinine level, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes.

estimate.span: The relative risk of the primary outcome was 30% lower in the canagliflozin group than in the placebo group, with event rates of 43.2 and 61.2 per 1000 patient-years, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.70; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.59 to 0.82; P = 0.00001).

analysis_set.span: The Intent-to-treat (ITT) population consisted of all randomized participants.

treatment_strategy.span: In this double-blind, randomized trial, we assigned patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric chronic kidney disease to receive canagliflozin, an oral SGLT2 inhibitor, at a dose of 100 mg daily or placebo.

follow_up.span: At that time, 4401 patients had undergone randomization, with a median follow-up of 2.62 years.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The randomized population had type 2 diabetes and albuminuric CKD, within the question's CKD population; registry eligibility specifies a minimum age of 30 years.

notes: Analysis-set binding uses the registry primary-outcome population statement. The abstract states that all patients received renin-angiotensin system blockade.
